# Battery replacement dates

Keeping this separate from the inventory because the dates matter on their own and
get lost in a document that's mostly about firmware and mast heights. Every entry
here is a battery that was actually swapped out, not just topped up or tested.

AWS-11 was the first one changed, back in October 2025, only a few weeks after it
went in. The original battery never seemed to hold charge properly even in good
weather, which in hindsight looks like a unit that was faulty from new rather than
anything about the site; the replacement has behaved normally since.

AWS-02 and AWS-05 both had their batteries changed in December 2025, within the same
week of each other. Both were showing voltage sagging further than expected overnight
during a cold spell, well before either one had done a winter's worth of hard use,
and swapping them rather than waiting to see if they recovered was the more cautious
call given how hard both sites are to reach once the tracks turn to mud.

AWS-07's battery was replaced in January 2026, on the 17th, after it turned out to be
the actual cause of that station's eleven-day outage rather than the radio fault
everyone assumed at first. That one had probably been marginal for a while before it
finally gave out; nothing in the run-up flagged it clearly enough to catch early.

AWS-03 had its battery changed in April 2026, this time as a precaution rather than a
failure - it was reading a little lower than the rest of the group on a routine check
and got swapped before it became a repeat of the AWS-07 situation rather than after.

Four replacements in seven months, and no two for quite the same reason: one likely
faulty from new, two ahead of a cold spell, one after it had already caused an
outage, and one on a precaution. Worth checking this list before assuming a station's
original battery is still in there.
